title: Fractional Blood Pressure across Childhood and Adolescence: Age-Related Patterns and Potential Relevance to Pediatric Hypertension
content: Background/Objectives: Fractional blood pressure (FBP), calculated as FBP (%) = (pulse pressure/systolic pressure) × 100 and expressed as a percentage, may provide a proportional measure of vascular function, but its behavior across childhood remains unclear. This study characterized age-related FBP patterns in children and adolescents. Methods: FBP was calculated from published pediatric blood pressure reference data for children aged 1–17 years and analyzed by age group, sex, and blood-pressure categories. Severe hypertension was defined as systolic blood pressure at or above the 95th percentile plus 12 mm Hg. Results: FBP declined in early childhood, from 52% to 40% in boys and from 50% to 40% in girls. At blood pressure values corresponding to the severe-hypertension threshold, FBP declined from 42% to 31% in boys and from 37% to 31% in girls. From later childhood through adolescence, FBP remained relatively stable, approximately 40%–42% in boys and 39%–41% in girls, while calculated values in adolescents at the severe-hypertension threshold were consistently lower, at approximately 34% in boys and 33% in girls. Conclusions: FBP declines during early childhood and subsequently stabilizes despite increasing absolute blood pressure. FBP at the severe-hypertension threshold remained consistently lower than normotensive values. These findings suggest that FBP may be influenced by age-dependent vascular properties, including arterial compliance and impedance.
